mainTopic: The search for the רבנן's source of עשה דוחה לא תעשה: attempted proofs from a מצורע's shaving (ראשו, זקנו, and נזיר), each rejected
overview: The גמרא learned עשה דוחה לא תעשה from ציצית overriding כלאים, but that proof works only for the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל. So it asks where the רבנן learn the rule. First it tries the word "ראשו" by a מצורע: he shaves his head even though הקפת הראש is forbidden. That proof falls, because the לאו of הקפה does not apply to everyone, since women are not included. Next it tries "זקנו": a כהן מצורע shaves his beard. The גמרא argues the word is extra and so teaches about a לאו השוה בכל, but then shows the word is needed, because כהנים might have been treated more strictly. Then it tries another תנא's reading of "ראשו": a מצורע who is a נזיר shaves. This fails too, because a נזיר can cancel his vow through שאלה, the same reason we never learn from נזיר that an עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה ועשה. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a new answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier proof only works for one opinion, so where do the רבנן learn it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that learning עשה דוחה לא תעשה from ציצית and כלאים works only for the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, and asks for the source according to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל. But the רבנן, where do they learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the proof it just gave fits only one opinion. It now asks where the other opinion, the רבנן, gets the rule that a positive מצוה pushes aside a prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof depended on the view of תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל that every 'garment' in the תורה means wool or linen, which leaves a word in the פסוק free to teach that ציצית overrides כלאים. The רבנן do not hold this view, so for them that word is not free. They need a different source for עשה דוחה לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well / that is fine for
The תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל
The Sages, the majority opinion
From where do they learn it?

phrases.english: This works out well according to the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל.
According to the רבנן, from where do they learn it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule that a positive מצוה pushes aside a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח לְתַנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל. לְרַבָּנַן, מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new search for a source, after the proof from the previous part of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for עשה דוחה לא תעשה that works for the רבנן, who do not accept the reading of תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: The רבנן learn it from the word 'his head' about the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn the rule from "ראשו" in the shaving of a מצורע. A ברייתא explains that this word teaches that the מצורע shaves his head even though הקפת הראש is normally forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from "his head." As a ברייתא teaches: Why does the פסוק say "his head"? Because it says, "Do not round the corners of your head," I might think a מצורע is also included in this ban. So the פסוק says "his head."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן learn the rule from the shaving of a מצורע, and brings a ברייתא to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says the מצורע shaves 'all his hair,' so the extra word 'his head' seems unnecessary. The ברייתא says this word is there to teach that the מצורע must shave his head even though doing so breaks the לאו of rounding the corners. That is a positive מצוה pushing aside a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn it from
As a ברייתא teaches
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
A person with צרעת, who must shave when he becomes pure
The corners of your head

phrases.english: They learn it from "his head."
As it is taught: "His head" — why does the verse need to say it?
phrases.notes: The same פסוק already says the מצורע shaves all his hair, so 'his head' looks extra.

phrases.english: Because it is stated:
"You shall not round the corners of your head,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:27. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: I would think that a leper is also included in this,
therefore the verse says: "His head."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with a new source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn עשה דוחה לא תעשה from the extra word "ראשו": the מצורע's מצוה to shave pushes aside the לאו of rounding the corners.

steps.title: This תנא holds that shaving the whole head counts as rounding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that this ברייתא holds that shaving the entire head is also called הקפה, so the מצורע really is breaking the לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא holds that rounding the whole head is called rounding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains a hidden assumption in the ברייתא, which is needed for the proof to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the ban is only on removing the corners while leaving the rest of the hair. If so, a מצורע who shaves everything would break no ban, and there would be no proof. This תנא holds that shaving the whole head also counts as הקפה, so the מצורע's מצוה truly pushes aside a לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: And he holds
Rounding off, shaving the corners of the head
The entire head

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the מצורע only shaves the corners. He shaves everything, and the חידוש here is that shaving everything still counts as breaking the ban on הקפה.

phrases.english: And this תנא holds
that rounding the entire head is called rounding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the assumption that makes the proof in step 2 work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this תנא, shaving the entire head is included in the לאו of הקפה.

steps.title: The proof is rejected: the rounding ban does not apply to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the לאו of הקפה is special because it does not apply to all people, so we cannot learn from it that a מצוה pushes aside every לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: What about the ban on rounding? It is special, because it is a לאו that does not apply equally to everyone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the מצורע by pointing out something special about the ban on rounding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on הקפה does not apply to women, so it is a 'weaker' לאו. Maybe only such a לאו can be pushed aside by a positive מצוה. We cannot use it to prove that a positive מצוה pushes aside a לאו that applies to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: This can be refuted
What about this case, which is special because
A prohibition
Applies equally to everyone

steps.whatToRemember: The מצורע source fails because the לאו of הקפה does not apply to everyone. So the search for the רבנן's source of עשה דוחה לא תעשה continues.
steps.whyThisMatters: This pattern shows how the גמרא checks a proof: a source only works if nothing special about it could explain the result.

phrases.english: This can be refuted:
What about the prohibition of rounding?
It is special, because it is a prohibition that does not apply equally to all!
phrases.notes: Women are not included in the ban on rounding the corners of the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source offered in steps 2 and 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the מצורע's shaving as a general source for עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The לאו of הקפה does not apply to everyone (women are not included), so it may be easier to push aside than a לאו that applies to all.

steps.title: A new source: the word 'his beard' by a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the rule comes from זקנו. A ברייתא teaches that a כהן who is a מצורע shaves his beard, even though כהנים are normally forbidden to shave the corners of the beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes from 'his beard.' As a ברייתא teaches: why does the verse say 'his beard'? Since it says about כהנים, 'They shall not shave the corners of their beard,' I might think a כהן who is a מצורע also may not shave. So the verse says 'his beard,' to tell us he does shave.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from ראשו was rejected, so the גמרא offers a new source: the word זקנו in the shaving of a מצורע. A ברייתא shows that this word lets a כהן מצורע shave his beard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of the מצורע to shave pushes aside the לאו of כהנים not to shave the beard. This is a fresh case of עשה דוחה לא תעשה. But we still need to see whether it can teach about a לאו that applies to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: His beard. Here it is the word in the מצורע's shaving that the ברייתא explains.
I might have understood. This is the mistaken idea the verse comes to correct.
A כהן who has צרעת

phrases.english: Rather: it is derived from "his beard."
phrases.notes: This is the same shaving פסוק of the מצורע (ויקרא 14:9), which also mentions his beard.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "His beard" — why does the verse need to say it?
Since it is stated:
"And the corners of their beard they shall not shave,"

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אַף כֹּהֵן מְצוֹרָע כֵּן
phrases.english: I would think that even a כהן who is a מצורע is the same
so the verse says "his beard."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from ראשו (step 4) with a new source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is זקנו: a כהן מצורע shaves his beard despite the לאו for כהנים.

steps.title: Since the word is extra, apply it to a prohibition that applies to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that we already know a מצוה pushes aside a לאו that does not apply to all. So זקנו must be teaching that it also pushes aside a לאו that applies to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is not needed to teach about a לאו that does not apply to everyone, use it to teach about a לאו that applies to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how זקנו can reach the bigger rule. Since we don't need it for the smaller lesson, we move it to the bigger lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beard לאו of כהנים is itself a לאו that does not apply to all. We already know from ראשו (step 2) that a מצוה pushes aside that kind of לאו. Step 4 only stopped ראשו from teaching about every לאו. So this word would be repeating something we know, and the גמרא uses it for a לאו השוה בכל instead.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this matter. This is a rule for moving an extra teaching to a different topic.
Apply it to a different matter
A prohibition that applies equally to all people

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא itself says this. The ברייתא only spoke about a כהן מצורע. The jump to a לאו השוה בכל is the גמרא's own reasoning, based on the word being extra.

phrases.english: And if it is not needed for the matter
of a prohibition that does not apply to everyone,
phrases.notes: We already have that lesson from ראשו and הקפת הראש, back in step 2.

phrases.english: apply it to the matter
of a prohibition that applies to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְלָאו שֶׁאֵין שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the זקנו derivation reaches the bigger rule, answering the problem raised in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That a מצוה pushes aside even a לאו השוה בכל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word זקנו, which is not needed for a לאו that does not apply to all

steps.title: The word is still needed because כהנים might have been stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. זקנו is not extra, since without it we might think כהנים are different and a מצוה can't push aside even a limited לאו for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still needed. You might have thought: כהנים are different. Since the תורה gave them extra מצוות, a מצוה would not push aside even a לאו that does not apply to everyone. So the verse teaches us that it does push it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 6 by showing that זקנו teaches something real for כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since כהנים have more מצוות, we might treat their לאוין more strictly. Then the lesson of ראשו would not cover them. So זקנו is needed just to teach that the rule works for כהנים too, and nothing is left over to teach about a לאו השוה בכל.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is still needed. The word has its own job, so it is not extra.
It would enter your mind to say. This brings in the mistaken idea.
Extra מצוות given to כהנים
It teaches us

phrases.english: But it is still needed,
for it would enter your mind to say:
כהנים are different,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְרִיבָּה בָּהֶן הַכָּתוּב מִצְוֹת יְתֵירוֹת,
phrases.english: since the Torah gave them extra מצוות,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לָאו שֶׁאֵין שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל לָא דָּחֵי,
phrases.english: it would not push aside even a prohibition that does not apply to everyone,
phrases.notes: The thing doing the pushing is the מצורע's מצוה to shave.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that it does push it aside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'extra word' reasoning of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from זקנו for a לאו השוה בכל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: זקנו is not extra. It is needed to show that the rule applies even to כהנים, who might have been treated more strictly.

steps.title: Another source: 'his head' read as teaching about a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now uses a different תנא's reading of ראשו. He says the word teaches that a מצורע who is a נזיר still shaves his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes from 'his head,' as this other תנא reads it. As a ברייתא teaches: why does the verse say 'his head'? Since it says about a נזיר, 'No razor shall pass over his head,' I might think a מצורע who is a נזיר also may not shave. So the verse says 'his head,' to tell us he does shave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the זקנו idea and offers a new source: a ברייתא that reads ראשו as being about a נזיר. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, ראשו was read as being about הקפת הראש. This תנא reads the same word differently: the מצורע's מצוה to shave pushes aside the לאו of a נזיר not to shave. The case of נזיר is now the base for the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Of this other תנא, who reads the word differently
No razor shall pass over his head. This is the לאו of a נזיר.
A person who took a vow of נזירות and may not cut his hair

phrases.english: Rather, it is derived from "his head," as this other תנא reads it.
phrases.notes: Same word as in step 2, but this תנא learns a different lesson from it.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "His head" — why does the verse need to say it?

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״תַּעַר לֹא יַעֲבוֹר עַל רֹאשׁוֹ״,
phrases.english: Since it is stated: "No razor shall pass over his head,"

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אַף מְצוֹרָע וְנָזִיר כֵּן,
phrases.english: I would think that even a מצורע who is a נזיר is the same,
so the verse says: "his head."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting זקנו in step 7, the גמרא offers a new reading of ראשו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ראשו as this תנא reads it: a מצורע who is a נזיר shaves his head despite the לאו of נזירות.

steps.title: The נזיר proof is rejected because a נזיר can cancel his vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from a נזיר who is a מצורע. A נזיר's prohibition is weaker, since he can ask a חכם to cancel his vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: a נזיר who is a מצורע is different, because he can ask to have his vow cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the proof from step 8. It says the case of a נזיר is special, so we cannot learn a general rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר's ban on shaving exists only because of a vow he chose to take, and a חכם can undo that vow through שאלה. A prohibition that can be removed this easily is weaker than other לאוין. So the fact that an עשה pushes it aside proves nothing about stronger, permanent לאוין.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who is also a מצורע (and so must shave)
He can ask a חכם to cancel his vow

phrases.english: There is room to refute:
What about a נזיר who is a מצורע? He is different
since he can ask to undo his vow.
phrases.notes: "Asking" means going to a חכם, who can cancel the vow. Then the ban on shaving is gone completely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְנָזִיר מְצוֹרָע שֶׁכֵּן יֶשְׁנוֹ בִּשְׁאֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 8 from ראשו (a נזיר who is a מצורע).
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from נזיר. It does not reject the rule that an עשה pushes aside a לאו.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A נזיר's prohibition can be removed through שאלה, so it is weaker than other לאוין and cannot teach about all of them.

steps.title: Support for the rejection: otherwise an accepted rule would be contradicted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its rejection. We hold that an עשה does not push aside a לאו that comes with an עשה. If נזיר were a valid source, we would learn the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you don't say that נזיר is a weaker case, then our accepted rule that an עשה does not push aside a לא תעשה together with an עשה would be challenged. Let us learn the opposite from נזיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the claim in step 9. If we don't treat נזיר as a weaker case, it would clash with a rule we already hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר has both a לאו against shaving and an עשה to let his hair grow. Yet a מצורע's מצוה to shave pushes aside both of them. If נזיר could teach general rules, it would prove that an עשה pushes aside לא תעשה ועשה, which goes against what we hold.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold; this is an accepted rule

keyTerms.term: אֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה
keyTerms.meaning: An עשה does not push aside a לאו that comes together with an עשה
Let us learn (derive) from it

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
then that which we hold,
that a positive מצוה does not push aside
a prohibition together with a positive מצוה,
let us learn the opposite from נזיר!
phrases.notes: A נזיר has both a לאו against shaving and an עשה to grow his hair, yet the מצורע's shaving overrides both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the rejection in step 9 by showing that treating נזיר as a normal case leads to a contradiction.
steps.raayaObject: That נזיר is a weaker case and cannot be used to learn general rules.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted rule that אין עשה דוחה לא תעשה ועשה, which the נזיר case would otherwise contradict.

steps.title: Since we never learn from נזיר, we cannot learn this rule from it either
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees we don't learn from נזיר, because of שאלה. That same weakness also blocks the proof that an עשה pushes aside a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why don't we learn from נזיר that an עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה ועשה? Because a נזיר can cancel his vow. For the same reason, we cannot learn from נזיר that an עשה pushes aside a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the argument. The same reason that stops us from learning one rule from נזיר also stops us from learning the rule we are looking for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weakness of שאלה is a single reason that disqualifies נזיר as a source for anything. So whether the question is about לא תעשה ועשה or a plain לאו, נזיר cannot be the proof. The next step starts a new answer for the source that an עשה pushes aside a general לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
We do not learn (derive)
So too; the same applies here

steps.whatToRemember: The case of a נזיר who is a מצורע cannot prove that an עשה pushes aside a לאו. A נזיר's prohibition is weak, because his vow can be cancelled through שאלה.

phrases.english: Rather, from נזיר, what is the reason
that we do not learn?
Because there is room to refute,
since he can ask to undo his vow.
So too here, there is room to refute,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the proof from step 8, that an עשה pushes aside a לאו.

phrases.english: since he can ask to undo his vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִנָּזִיר מַאי טַעְמָא לָא גָּמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the contradiction raised in step 10 and applies the same answer to the current proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נזיר cannot serve as a source for whether an עשה pushes aside a לאו, because his prohibition can be removed through שאלה.

steps.title: A new approach begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the נזיר proof and opens a new explanation with "Rather, actually."
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new answer, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from נזיר has fallen, so the גמרא goes back to look for a different source. The word לעולם ("actually") usually signals a return to an earlier idea, read in a new way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (switching to a new approach)
Actually; really (often returning to an earlier idea)

phrases.english: Rather, actually...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the נזיר proof is rejected, this opens a fresh attempt to find the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the opening words appear here; the new explanation continues on the next amud.
